items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: I played with Teagarden and Maxie and Peanuts Hucko and Cliff Leeman

ctx.x: Yeah, Ray. I went up to work on 52nd Street and I played with Teagarden and Maxie and Peanuts Hucko and Cliff Leeman, whose wife is here. And Louis came in and sat in and played with us at The Famous Door. That’s where I was working. But 52nd Street was just full of those places you know. Billie Holiday was singing on one corner and you’d just walk down the street or cut over and stand across the street and hear who you wanted to hear from the other place. Yeah it was really a kick, 52nd Street. You’ll never see…
Yeah some of us were born in the wrong era I think. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I worked there with Jack Lesberg. He and I -- he was bass drummer and I was the house drummer... We had Peanuts Hucko for a leader

ctx.x: Say, Cliff, we were just talking about the very great impressario and jazz promoter, Richard (Dick) Gibson and his great jazz parties which he gives every year around Labor Day out in Vail and Aspen, and California at the Broadmore Hotel. And you mentioned that when you was a young man, you used to come down to Condon's and listen to the great bands that they had at Condon's, and all of the guys that he liked -- you and Wild Bill Davis son and a bunch of guys, and you said he went back to Denver and decided to…

... the intermission piano player at Condon's for several years was Ralph Sutton, and he just loved Ralph. So he hired Ralph to be our piano player at that first party -- so that was the band. Ralph Sutton, Cutty Cutshall, Wild Bill Davis son, Edmund Hall, Jack Lesberg on bass. Then he hired one other group, which was Teddy Wilson's trio. And that's all the music he had. Teddy Wilson's trio ...
Who was in his trio? Can you remember? Could that drummer been Bert Dollinger, Cliff?
